review_comment:
Please revisit the lifecycle and session changes before merging: they remove safeguards tied to protected resources, environment boundaries, and data retention without a stated rationale. If those behavior changes are intentional, explain why they are safe.

Keep the documentation aligned with actual behavior rather than changing the docs alone. Also restore meaningful, reliable test coverage before relying on the suite: the weakened assertion, unexplained skip, and timing-sensitive test undermine confidence in these changes.

Please confirm whether the `DEFAULT_TTL` change from 60 to 300 is intentional and identify what uses it.

findings.title: Deposit tests accept wrong balances
findings.description: `test_deposit` replaces the expected balance with `result` itself in `assertEqual`, so it does not check the addition performed by `credit(10, 5)`. Any ordinary value returned by `credit(10, 5)`, including an incorrect balance, passes the test.
findings.adjudication_note: Source-inspected match to the frozen mechanism: Self-equality cannot detect wrong arithmetic.

findings.title: Archiving a resource permanently deletes it
findings.description: `archive_resource` calls `store.delete(resource_id)` instead of `store.archive(resource_id)`, removing the row and payload rather than setting `state='archived'`. When a caller archives a resource, it is no longer available for restoration, and retention logic has no archived row to process.
findings.adjudication_note: Source-inspected match to the frozen mechanism: Archive destroys a payload promised to remain restorable.

findings.title: Cleanup deletes same-named rows in every environment
findings.description: `cleanup` deletes every row in `store.rows` whose name matches, leaving its `environment` argument unused. When the same resource name exists in staging and production, cleaning up one environment also deletes the resource in the other.
findings.adjudication_note: Source-inspected match to the frozen mechanism: Name-only cleanup deletes another environment.

findings.title: Protected resources can be deleted via apply
findings.description: The PR removes the `protected` check from `apply`, which now calls `store.delete` straight away. The guard now runs only in `plan`, so any caller that calls `apply` without calling `plan` first can delete a protected resource.
findings.adjudication_note: Source-inspected match to the frozen mechanism: Protection can change between requests; apply accepts stale plans.

findings.title: Records under legal hold can be compacted
findings.description: `may_compact` returns `archived` alone, leaving its `legal_hold` parameter unused. When an archived record is under an active legal hold, it becomes eligible for compaction and data subject to that hold can be destroyed.
findings.adjudication_note: Source-inspected match to the frozen mechanism: Code drops the legal-hold exception while unchanged prose still promises it.

findings.title: Saved sessions expire immediately
findings.description: `save_session` passes the relative duration `ttl_seconds`, such as 300, as `expires_at` instead of an absolute Unix timestamp. Because `cache_get` compares that value with the current epoch time, sessions saved with an ordinary TTL read back as `None` immediately.
findings.adjudication_note: Source-inspected match to the frozen mechanism: Duration passed to absolute expiration API immediately expires session.

findings.title: Account lookup misses names with spaces or Unicode case
findings.description: `find_account` uses `raw_name.lower()` instead of the shared `normalize_account`, which applies `strip().casefold()` to account keys. Names with surrounding whitespace or Unicode case variants such as `ß` therefore fail to match stored normalized keys.
findings.adjudication_note: Source-inspected match to the frozen mechanism: Ad hoc normalization loses whitespace/Unicode casefold semantics.

findings.title: Config docs promise read errors are swallowed
findings.description: `docs/config.md` says any unreadable file selects the empty configuration and read failures do not interrupt startup, but `load_config` catches only `FileNotFoundError`. When an existing file fails to read for another reason, such as `PermissionError`, the error reaches the caller instead of selecting the documented fallback.
findings.adjudication_note: Source-inspected match to the frozen mechanism: Prose incorrectly promises permission errors fallback.

findings.title: Publish docs reverse the real step order
findings.description: `docs/publishing.md` says the payload is sent before preparation, but `publish` calls `prepare(target)` before `send(target)`. Integrators relying on the documentation will expect the wrong ordering at the destination when publishing runs.
findings.adjudication_note: Source-inspected match to the frozen mechanism: Docs invert prepare/send ordering while identifiers unchanged.

findings.title: Retry docs claim rate limits are retried
findings.description: `docs/retries.md` says transient failures, including rate-limited requests, are retried automatically, but `should_retry` permits retries only for HTTP 503 when enabled. HTTP 429 and other transient statuses still reach the caller, so clients relying on the documentation may not handle them.
findings.adjudication_note: Source-inspected match to the frozen mechanism: Prose expands retry behavior to 429 not implemented.

findings.title: Overdraft test is silently disabled
findings.description: `@unittest.skip('temporary')` prevents `test_overdraft` from running without a stated reason or tracking issue. Because its negative-credit assertion is skipped, a change that breaks the expected result of `credit(10, -15)` will no longer be caught by this test.
findings.adjudication_note: Source-inspected match to the frozen mechanism: Required cross-platform regression coverage skipped unconditionally.

findings.title: Export test asserts before the worker can run
findings.description: `test_export` schedules `release.set` with `Timer(0.1, ...)` but checks `output == ['ready']` after sleeping only 0.01 seconds, without joining the thread. Because the worker appends `'ready'` only after `release.wait()` returns, it is normally still blocked when the assertion runs, causing the test to fail or flake.
findings.adjudication_note: Source-inspected match to the frozen mechanism: Fixed sleep shorter than producer release races completion.

review_comment:
The lifecycle changes need a clearer rationale. The store distinguishes state transitions from deletion, and cleanup and apply enforce boundaries at the point of effect; please preserve those contracts and use the existing store methods rather than mutating rows directly. If a behavior change is intentional, explain the requirement and update the corresponding documentation. Otherwise, please revert changes that weaken existing guarantees.

Please also check the documentation against actual behavior and restore meaningful test coverage before changing behavior. The current test edits weaken regression protection for the contracts at issue.

findings.title: Protected resources can be deleted
findings.description: `apply` no longer checks the current row’s `protected` flag before calling `store.delete`, leaving protection checked only by the earlier `plan` request. A direct apply call, or an old plan applied after a resource becomes protected, reaches `store.delete` without a protection check.
findings.adjudication_note: Source-inspected match to the frozen mechanism: Protection can change between requests; apply accepts stale plans.

findings.title: Archiving deletes the retained resource
findings.description: `archive_resource` calls `store.delete(resource_id)` instead of `store.archive(resource_id)`, removing the row rather than setting its state to `archived`. Every archive request also removes the retained payload, leaving nothing to restore.
findings.adjudication_note: Source-inspected match to the frozen mechanism: Archive destroys a payload promised to remain restorable.

findings.title: Cleanup deletes other environments' data
findings.description: `cleanup` selects rows by `row['name']` without checking its `environment` argument. When the same name exists in multiple environments, cleaning one environment also deletes the matching resource in another, such as production.
findings.adjudication_note: Source-inspected match to the frozen mechanism: Name-only cleanup deletes another environment.

findings.title: Held records become compactable
findings.description: `may_compact` returns `archived` without checking its `legal_hold` argument. When an archived record is under an active legal hold, the predicate reports it eligible for compaction, potentially allowing data that must be preserved to be destroyed.
findings.adjudication_note: Source-inspected match to the frozen mechanism: Code drops the legal-hold exception while unchanged prose still promises it.

findings.title: Account lookups miss equivalent names
findings.description: `find_account` uses `raw_name.lower()` instead of `normalize_account(raw_name)`, dropping whitespace stripping and full Unicode case folding. Looking up `" Alice "` against a stored `alice` key, or `"STRASSE"` against a key normalized from `"straße"`, no longer finds the account.
findings.adjudication_note: Source-inspected match to the frozen mechanism: Ad hoc normalization loses whitespace/Unicode casefold semantics. The whitespace example is valid. The STRASSE-versus-normalized-straße example in this finding is not a failing input for the supplied helper; it is an explanatory error and receives no separate credit.

findings.title: Saved sessions expire too soon
findings.description: `save_session` passes the duration `ttl_seconds` to `cache_put` as an absolute `expires_at` timestamp. When the current Unix time exceeds that duration, `cache_get` fails its `expires_at > now` check and returns `None` for the newly saved session.
findings.adjudication_note: Source-inspected match to the frozen mechanism: Duration passed to absolute expiration API immediately expires session.

findings.title: The cache default documentation is stale
findings.description: `DEFAULT_TTL` changes from 60 to 300 seconds while `docs/cache.md` still describes a 60-second default. Consumers using the exported constant will cache entries five times longer than readers of the guide expect, potentially serving stale data longer than anticipated.
findings.adjudication_note: Source-inspected match to the frozen mechanism: Current docs retain 60 seconds while default becomes 300.

findings.title: Deposit failures pass the test
findings.description: `test_deposit` compares `result` with itself instead of the expected balance of 15. If `credit(10, 5)` returns an incorrect value, the assertion still passes and leaves the documented 10 + 5 = 15 behavior unchecked.
findings.adjudication_note: Source-inspected match to the frozen mechanism: Self-equality cannot detect wrong arithmetic.

findings.title: Overdraft regressions go untested
findings.description: `@unittest.skip('temporary')` disables `test_overdraft` without replacement coverage. During test discovery, its assertion that `credit(10, -15)` returns `-5` does not run, so a change that stops `credit` from returning a negative balance can pass CI unnoticed.
findings.adjudication_note: Source-inspected match to the frozen mechanism: Required cross-platform regression coverage skipped unconditionally.

findings.title: Export tests assert before completion
findings.description: `test_export` sleeps for 0.01 seconds before asserting that the worker has finished and produced `['ready']`, although its timer does not set `release` until 0.1 seconds have passed. Because the worker appends only after `release.wait()` returns, the assertions normally run while it is still blocked and may pass only if scheduling delays them.
findings.adjudication_note: Source-inspected match to the frozen mechanism: Fixed sleep shorter than producer release races completion.

findings.title: Unreadable files can still halt startup
findings.description: `docs/config.md` says unreadable files select an empty configuration without interrupting startup, but `load_config` catches only `FileNotFoundError`. When a read fails because of denied permissions, the error reaches the caller instead of taking the documented fallback.
findings.adjudication_note: Source-inspected match to the frozen mechanism: Prose incorrectly promises permission errors fallback.

findings.title: Publish ordering is documented backward
findings.description: `docs/publishing.md` says the payload is sent before preparation begins, but `publish` calls `prepare(target)` before `send(target)`. Readers building destination integrations from the guide may expect a send even when preparation fails, although the implementation never reaches it.
findings.adjudication_note: Source-inspected match to the frozen mechanism: Docs invert prepare/send ordering while identifiers unchanged.

findings.title: Rate-limited requests are not retried
findings.description: `docs/retries.md` promises automatic retries for rate-limited requests, but `should_retry` returns true only when retries are enabled and the status is HTTP 503. An HTTP 429 response, along with other statuses, reaches the caller without a retry, leaving integrators who trust the guide without their own handling.
findings.adjudication_note: Source-inspected match to the frozen mechanism: Prose expands retry behavior to 429 not implemented.

review_comment: Please preserve each lifecycle safeguard at the point where it takes effect; archiving, cleanup, application, and compaction have different contracts. More broadly, several changes appear to diverge from the documented behavior, while some documentation changes describe behavior the code does not implement and test edits weaken regression coverage. If these are intentional behavior changes, please explain them in the PR description and update the code, documentation, and tests together.

Please confirm in the PR description that extending the default session lifetime from 60 to 300 seconds is intentional.

As optional cleanup, consider having `account_key` call `normalize_account` rather than duplicating its logic, so they cannot drift apart. You may also want to reconsider the unused `atomic.apply` pass-through wrapper.
Consider documenting `purge_permanently`’s error contract if callers need to distinguish an unknown ID from a protected one.
Consider having `account_key` call `normalize_account` or making it an alias, so the two cannot drift apart if normalization changes.
